newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Pakistani named U.N. special envoy for East Timor.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani named U.N. special envoy for East Timor.

text.p: Pakistan's former U.N. envoy, Jamsheed Marker, was appointed on Wednesday as Secretary-General Kofi Annan's personal representative for East Timor, the former Portuguese territory whose annexation by Indonesia two decades ago remains a matter of contention.
Marker, 74, retired in March 1995 after more than four years as his country's U.N. ambassador.

The United Nations has never recognised Indonesia's 1976 annexation of East Timor, which it invaded the previous year after the departure of Portugal, the colonial power. Talks aimed at finding an internationally acceptable solution were initiated by then-Secretary-General Javier Perez de Cuellar in 1983 and continued by his successor, Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

In announcing Marker's appointment, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said it was part of Annan's effort to give impetus to finding a "just, comprehensive and internationally acceptable solution to the question of East Timor."

While the new secretary-general intended to be personally engaged in these efforts, he had asked Marker to represent him in all aspects of his good offices function, including talks under U.N. auspices between Indonesia and Portugal. He would also be involved in consultations that the secretary-general holds with a cross-section of East Timorese figures.

The eighth round of long-running talks between the foreign ministers of Indonesia and Portugal took place in Geneva last June under Boutros-Ghali. A ninth round had been scheduled for December but was postponed.

Annan held separate exploratory meetings this month with Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas and Portuguese Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Vitorino on the fringes of the World Economic Forum at Davos, Switzerland.
